The project scope includes OA, LSOA, MSOA, local-authority types, council areas, combined authorities, metropolitan geographies and regions. This first version shows the official snapshots already indexed and the history still to audit.

Indexed boundary vintages, 2010–2026

A tick means at least one source release is indexed for that vintage. A dash means none is indexed: it does not mean the area was abolished or its boundary changed. Census boundaries often remain in use between census revisions.

Dates here describe source vintages, not certified annual legal validity. Pre-2010 products, including 2001 census boundaries, can be shown in Find files. Scottish and Northern Irish census ingestion is part of the project scope.

Official geography downloads

Why 2010 needs special treatment

The current indexed local-authority collection has no file explicitly labelled 2010. The 2009 and 2011 releases are available as reference vintages, but neither is automatically certified as the boundary at a date in 2010.

Small-area data reported in 2010 may use 2001 census geography. Keep the date of your statistics separate from the vintage of their boundaries.

What changed?

A complete history needs separate records for name/code changes, council reorganisations, legal boundary changes and geometry revisions.

The ONS Code History Database supplies codes, relationships, dates and archived geography metadata. It complements the polygon files.

Kirklees, decoded

E08000034 · Metropolitan district · West Yorkshire. Kirklees has a single-tier metropolitan council. It is classified separately from an E06 unitary authority. It is within West Yorkshire metropolitan county, and is a constituent council of the West Yorkshire Combined Authority, founded in 2014.

“Metropolitan area” can refer to different administrative or functional geographies. The explorer keeps metropolitan districts, metropolitan counties and combined authorities distinct. Kirklees contains multiple MSOAs; those are a separate census reporting level.

Boundary detail explained
BFE · Full extent
Full resolution, extending to the extent of the realm.
BFC · Full clipped
Full resolution, clipped at mean high water.
BGC · Generalised clipped
Usually generalised to 20 metres; useful for maps. Check each product's specification.
BSC · Super generalised clipped
Usually generalised to 200 metres; useful for overview maps.

Keep detail and coastal treatment consistent when comparing years. ONS product guidance

Planned history and translation layer

Next: import code lineage, record legal effective dates, audit the 2010 baseline, ingest Scottish and Northern Irish census vintages, and add GeoPackage exports. A translation table should record source code/vintage, target code/vintage, relationship and weighting method.

Exact aggregation, best-fit assignment, area-weighted estimates and population-weighted estimates need distinct labels. A code lookup alone does not supply defensible population weights.
